title: Long-context burst throughput: INT8/AWQ/FP8 field notes (Feb 2028)
body:
Summary:

Quick field notes from a small benching pass that looked at how quantized kernels (INT8-GPTQ style, AWQ-derived int8, and FP8 paths) behave when we drive long-context workloads under bursty arrival patterns. Found surprising non-monotonic throughput regressions at large sequence lengths (8k+) for the FP8 path and a batch-shape sensitivity in the AWQ kernel that amplifies p99 latency under short bursts. This doc records what we ran, raw-ish numbers, profiling traces, hypotheses, and next steps.

Motivation / why this felt urgent:
- We are seeing customer reports where long-context agents (>=8k) degrade throughput when traffic spikes; they expect linear token amortization gains but observe bursts of high p99 latency.
- We need to know whether quant variant/kernels or runtime batching/KV handling is the main cause so we can recommend sensible routing/fallbacks.

Testbed (short):
- HW: 1x A100-80GB (DGX-like node), CUDA 12.1, cuBLAS/cuDNN latest on our bench image
- Runtime: serving-runtime @ commit 5b7c9a2 (branch: experimental/quant-burst-probes)
- Models: 13B dense baseline (FP16), GPTQ-int8 variant (gptq-true), AWQ-int8 variant (awq-opt), FP8-compiled variant (fp8-optim)
- Sequence lengths tested: 128, 1024, 8192, 16384 (generation 512 tokens after prefix)
- Arrival shapes: steady small (10 rps, concurrency 1), moderate sustained (50 rps), short burst (200 concurrent arriving within 2s, lasting 10s), sustained burst (50 concurrent for 60s)
- Clients: local bench harness + synthetic KV-cache enabled (key/value cache warm for repeated prompts in same conversation)

Metrics captured:
- tokens_per_sec (aggregate), mean latency (ms), p95, p99 latencies, GPU kernel breakdown (top3 kernels by time), memcpy host<->device times, KV copy times, allocator stalls (ms)

Representative results (raw) — generation of 512 tokens after prefix:
- seq=128:
  - FP16 baseline: 12.8k tokens/s, p95=42ms, p99=78ms
  - GPTQ-int8: 18.3k tokens/s, p95=34ms, p99=62ms
  - AWQ-int8: 17.9k tokens/s, p95=36ms, p99=64ms
  - FP8 path: 19.1k tokens/s, p95=33ms, p99=61ms
- seq=1024:
  - FP16: 8.6k t/s, p95=78ms, p99=140ms
  - GPTQ-int8: 11.9k t/s, p95=66ms, p99=120ms
  - AWQ-int8: 11.6k t/s, p95=69ms, p99=125ms
  - FP8: 12.3k t/s, p95=64ms, p99=118ms
- seq=8192 (key observations start to diverge):
  - FP16: 2.1k t/s, p95=320ms, p99=610ms
  - GPTQ-int8: 2.9k t/s, p95=290ms, p99=540ms
  - AWQ-int8: 2.8k t/s, p95=305ms, p99=620ms (spikey p99 under burst)
  - FP8: 2.1k t/s, p95=410ms, p99=920ms (FP8 lost its earlier advantage; p99 much worse)
- seq=16384:
  - FP16: 1.2k t/s, p95=760ms, p99=1480ms
  - GPTQ-int8: 1.6k t/s, p95=680ms, p99=1300ms
  - AWQ-int8: 1.55k t/s, p95=730ms, p99=1420ms
  - FP8: 0.95k t/s, p95=1010ms, p99=2200ms

Notes on arrival shapes (burst vs steady):
- Under steady traffic the FP8 path roughly tracked expectation (slightly faster than INT8 variants at small seq).
- Short bursts (200 concurrent) exposed oscillations in the FP8 runs: initial token throughput good, then after 3–6s p99 spikes dramatically and throughput drops to ~50% for the remainder of the burst window.
- AWQ-int8 shows batch-shape sensitivity: when many concurrent small requests arrive, the kernel chooses a different vectorization path that increases tail latency by ~25% compared to consolidated batching; this shows up most at seq>=1024.

Profiling extracts (topline, aggregated across run segments):
- FP8 path (seq=8192, during spike):
  - matmul_kernel_fp8_pack (kernel): 44% of GPU time
  - kv_cache_copy (memcpy/host<->device): 18%
  - aten_attention_fp8 (kernel): 16%
  - allocator stalls: aggregated 120ms per request (observed in runtime timeline)
- GPTQ-int8 (same segment):
  - matmul_int8_kernel: 36%
  - kv_cache_copy: 12%
  - aten_attention_int8: 14%
  - allocator stalls: ~45ms/request
- Memory profile: FP8 path had higher transient device memory usage (due to per-layer FP8 scaling tensors kept live) which triggered more frequent small allocations and frees; we see memcpy churn and occasional GC-like stalls in allocator.

Qualitative observations / surprises:
1) FP8's throughput advantage at short sequences does not translate to long-context steady bursts because of two interacting effects: (a) extra metadata + per-layer scaling buffers for FP8 increase device memory footprint and allocation churn; (b) FP8 kernels in our build trigger a different GEMM codepath that is less tolerant of large KV cache strides (cache footprint grows with seq) — combined they induce throttling and p99 blowups.
2) AWQ-int8 sensitivity seems tied to batch-shape detection heuristics. When the runtime forms many small micro-batches vs fewer consolidated batches, the AWQ kernel selects a narrower vector width to avoid register pressure, which is suboptimal for long vectors and amplifies latency.
3) GPTQ-int8 was the most robust across shapes; fewer transient allocations and a mature kernel path help (tradeoff: slightly lower peak tokens/s at tiny seqs vs FP8).

Hypotheses to validate (ranked):
- H1: Allocator churn + transient per-layer buffers in FP8 path cause host/device memcpy thrash when KV cache is large. Validate by forcing a pre-allocated buffer pool and re-running burst.
- H2: Kernel selection heuristics flip at thresholds of sequence length and batch shape; AWQ path heuristics are too eager to change vectorization for micro-batches. Validate by instrumenting kernel selection decisions and forcing single kernel choice.
- H3: Memory bandwidth thrash from KV copies becomes the bottleneck as sequence length grows; mitigating with on-GPU persistent KV or compressed KV reduces p99. Validate by enabling on-GPU KV and measuring delta.

Experiment notes (what I tried quickly):
- Prewarming: warming KV cache reduced cold-start jitter but did not prevent FP8 p99 spike during bursts.
- Force single-kernel flag: forcing FP8 to use the fast GEMM decreased p95 but did not eliminate the p99 spike — allocator stalls still present.
- Pre-alloc pool simulation: mocked a simple arena allocator reduced allocator stalls by ~40% and improved FP8 p99 by ~20% at seq=8192 under burst (promising).

Immediate action items (short list):
- Short-term (this week):
  1) Add instrumentation to record per-request allocator events + kernel selection decision in logs (INF-3297). Owner: Ethan.
  2) Run a focused pre-alloc arena test across FP8/GPTQ/AWQ variants with higher concurrency shapes (owner: Maya).
  3) Add an experimental config that forces GPTQ-int8 fallback for seq>8k for the hosted tier; monitor impact (owner: Jonas).
- Medium-term:
  4) Explore persistent on-GPU KV option for long-context workloads (bench and infra impact).
  5) Work with kernel authors to add a cost model for kernel selection that accounts for KV stride / device allocation pressure.

Open questions / things to log in follow-ups:
- Exact allocation patterns per-layer for FP8 (which tensors are kept live and why).
- Whether the FP8 GEMM codepath can be patched to be more tolerant of wide KV caches (likely low-level work).
- Is AWQ micro-batch heuristic configurable without sacrificing small-seq perf?

Notes to self / rough TODOs in order:
- instrument -> re-run arena -> collect traces -> open a small PR to expose a force-kernel flag to the service -> share a micro-bench run with solutions-engineering to check regressions for a customer use-case.

Appendix (fragile raw trace pointers):
- sample gfx trace: s3://bench-artifacts/quant/long-context/trace-2028-02-12-13-42.gz
- perf summary CSV: s3://bench-artifacts/quant/long-context/summary-2028-02-12.csv

If anyone else on call wants to pick next steps, flag here. My leaning: try the arena prealloc + kernel selection logging first; they are fast and high signal.

-- Maya
